sources.title: Jing'an Temple Shanghai Guide (2026): History, Culture & Tranquility
sources.content:
Jing'an Temple is one of Shanghai's oldest and largest Buddhist temples at 1686 Nanjing West Road. Origins trace to 247 CE during the Three Kingdoms period as Hudu Chongyuan Temple. Received current name in 1008 under the Song Dynasty. Relocated to present location in 1216, predating Shanghai's official establishment.

Hours: 7:30 AM - 5:00 PM daily. Admission: ¥50 per person (free for children under 120 cm; complimentary on 1st and 15th lunar days). Duration: 1-2 hours.

Dharma Hall: Seven-story, 32.22-meter structure with imported Burmese teak and copper-tiled roof. Mountain Gate: Two-story granite structure with teak doors. Bell Tower: Houses Peace Bell (3.3 meters, 7.3 tons) and the Spring Well, known as The Sixth Spring Under Heaven.

Guanyin Hall: Contains statue carved from single camphor wood piece. Mahavira Hall: Grand central structure with 15-ton silver Shakyamuni Buddha statue. Jing'an Pagoda: Seven-story with gold-leaf plating.

Spiritual Practices: Lighting incense bundles (¥10), making wishes bowing before main hall, tossing coins into Fortune and Wisdom Cauldron (10.23-meter, 15.5-ton bronze structure).

Nearby Dining: Ren He Guan (Yellow Croaker noodles), FINE FAN zakka, KLAY Modern Indian, Huxi Laonongtang Noodle House.

Transportation: Metro Lines 2 or 7 to Jing'an Temple Station (Exits 1 or 5).

sources.title: Shanghai Jing'an Temple - Where the Biggest Jade Buddha of China Is Enshrined
sources.content:
Shanghai Jing'an Temple houses the largest jade Buddha in China. Three main halls date from approximately 1880. The complex underwent reconstruction following a 1972 fire.

Two large modern buildings flank the main gate. The Ming Dynasty copper bell now resides in the main hall, alongside another bell cast in 1999.

Visitors encounter a large tripod shrine in a courtyard where people burn offerings and attempt tossing coins for good fortune. The site displays figures beyond Buddha, including historical figures and ancient Chinese deities from Daoism.

The temple name means tranquil and peaceful. During the Cultural Revolution, it functioned as a plastics factory. After the 1972 fire, reconstruction occurred in the 1980s, with reopening in the 1990s.

Location: Downtown Shanghai, adjacent to subway station (Line 2, Exit 1). Hours: 7 am to 5 pm. Entry Fee: Approximately 50 RMB (free on lunar calendar's 1st and 15th days).

sources.title: Guide to Jing'an Temple: History, Legends, and Must-See Treasures
sources.content:
Jing'an Temple is nestled at the heart of Shanghai's Jing'an District and stands as a serene oasis amid the city's nonstop buzz. Built over 1,700 years ago during the Three Kingdoms era.

Golden-tiled roofs and classic curved eaves. In Mahavira Hall, the biggest pure jade portrait of Sakyamuni in Mainland China: 3.78 meters height, 11,000 kilograms weight.

Early Morning (7:00–9:00): Quiet temple grounds with monks' chants. Sunset (17:00–18:00): Warm light bathes the gilded roofs as skyscrapers shimmer nearby.

Please wear modest clothing—no shorts, short skirts, or off-shoulder tops. Keep voice low. Do not bring your own incense. Purchase eco-friendly sticks at designated stalls.

Plan 1–2 hours. By metro: Line 2 or Line 7, Jing'an Temple Station. By bus: 15, 20, 40, 113, 315, 321, 330, 824, 830 or 927.

sources.title: Jing'an Temple 2026 - The China Journey
sources.content:
Jing'an Temple is one of Shanghai's most iconic landmarks, known for rich history, cultural significance, and architectural splendor. Located at 1686 West Nanjing Road, Jing'an District.

Ticket Price: 50 RMB on regular days; 100 RMB during holidays. Opening Hours: 7:30 AM – 5:00 PM. On 1st and 15th day of each lunar month, entry is free.

The jade Buddha has height of 3.78 meters and weight of 11,000 kilograms. An important display is the bronze bell made in the Ming Dynasty.

For exterior night viewing allocate 30–60 minutes. For interior visit plus temple meal, plan 2–3 hours. The temple offers vegetarian dining with a simple, elegant temple meal.

sources.title: 静安寺_百度百科
sources.content:
静安寺位于上海市静安区南京西路1686号，总建筑面积达2.2万平方米，上海市文物保护单位和汉族地区佛教全国重点寺院。

相传始建于三国吴大帝孙权赤乌十年（247年），创始人为康僧会。初名沪读重元寺，唐代改名永泰禅院，北宋大中祥符元年（1008年）始名静安寺。南宋嘉定九年（1216年）迁至今址，早于上海建城。

建筑采用宋营造法，布局严格在中轴线上。大雄宝殿高26米，供奉一尊15吨纯银铸造的释迦牟尼佛像。法堂共7层，高32.22米，采用缅甸柚木为主结构。静安宝塔为7层方形，建筑面积952平方米。

民国元年第一个全国性佛教组织中华佛教总会成立于此。1953年持松法师设立真言密宗坛场，复兴了自唐代失传的汉地佛教密宗。

寺内藏有八大山人名画、文征明真迹《琵琶行》行草长卷。历史上有八大名胜：赤乌碑、陈朝桧、虾子潭、讲经台、涌泉、绿云洞、芦子渡、沪渎垒。

2009年15吨纯银浇铸的如来佛祖银身像进驻寺内。

sources.title: Jing'an Temple – One of the Most Famous Temples in Shanghai
sources.content:
Jing'an Temple is one of the most famous temples in Shanghai, with a history spanning over 1,700 years. Located in the heart of the city's commercial district on West Nanjing Road.

The temple houses the largest jade Buddha statue in mainland China. The main halls feature traditional Chinese Buddhist architecture with golden roofs and intricate carvings.

Metro Line 2 or Line 7 to Jing'an Temple Station. Opening hours: 7:30 AM to 5:00 PM. Admission: 50 RMB. Free entry on the 1st and 15th of each lunar month.

Highlights include the Mahavira Hall with its jade Buddha, the bronze bell from the Ming Dynasty, and the seven-story pagoda.
